title: REHASH and the TLS certificate: may a client make the daemon reach off the machine?
description:
MARK'S CALL. Left out of mimid-1wgh.140.4, which implemented REHASH
over the configuration file alone.

The Modern IRC Client Protocol §"REHASH message" says a rehash "may
include other data, such as modules or TLS certificates", and the
certificate is the reload an operator is most likely to want after
their certbot has written a new pair. REHASH does not do it today:
crates/mimid-agent/src/tls.rs re-reads the certificate only in
`Tls::reload_loop`, which polls, so a new pair goes into use at the
next tick and not when the user asks.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE WITH THE VERB. `reload_loop` covers four sources
and only two of them stay on this machine. `files` and `local-ca` read
local files and are idempotent. `tailscale` asks tailscaled over its
local socket. `acme` can talk to a rate-limited certificate authority:
`acme::ensure` only orders past two thirds of the certificate's life,
so a loop cannot by itself hammer the authority, but once that point is
passed a failing order would be retried once per REHASH. A registered
IRC client can send REHASH as fast as it likes, and bead
mimid-1wgh.140.4 would not give a client a way to make the daemon reach
off the machine on that schedule without Mark saying so.

THE OPTIONS.
1. Nothing: the poll stays the only path. The operator's new
   certificate waits out RELOAD_FILES_EVERY.
2. `files` and `local-ca` on REHASH, `tailscale` and `acme` answered
   with a NOTICE saying where that certificate comes from and that it
   is renewed on its own timer. Keeps every REHASH local, needs no
   cooldown, and no test has to assert on a wall clock.
3. All four, with a cooldown. The cooldown is then a wall-clock fact a
   test would have to assert on.

WHAT IT COSTS EITHER WAY. The report REHASH sends is driven by the
diff of the file, so a certificate re-read that no key in the file
mentions needs a second line of output -- what was re-read
unconditionally -- or the user is told "nothing changed" while a new
leaf went into use. §7.38 says today that REHASH reads the
configuration file and nothing else, which is why its output needs no
such line; adding the certificate changes that sentence.

THE EXTRACTION IT NEEDS. `reload_loop`'s iteration body holds the
source match, the swap and the expiry complaint. The load belongs in a
method both callers share; the loop keeps its own mtime check, and
after a REHASH has loaded new files the loop's `seen` is stale and it
loads once more at its next tick, which is idempotent under the
`RwLock`. The tailscale arm indexes `self.setting.names[0]`, panic-free
only because `TlsSetting::check` requires a name for that source; a
socket-reachable caller should turn that into a `first()` match or
write the argument down at the call site.

Two settings named in the same breath, both out of mimid-1wgh.140.4:
the did:webvh log and witness files, which `LogWatch` re-reads before
each sync, so a REHASH could notify `Store::sync_wanted` and have the
changed log taken at once instead of at the next interval; and
`token_file`, the rotation an operator would want most, which is on the
needs-restart list only because `mimid_agent_core::Agent` has no token
setter.
